content: A dummy edit refers to a modification in the wikitext of a page that has little to no impact on how the page appears when rendered. However, it allows the editor to save a useful edit summary. This summary can serve various purposes, such as sending a text message to other editors or correcting a previous edit summary, for instance, if an earlier edit was mistakenly marked as minor. The edit summary can act as a communication tool, especially for editors who use IP addresses without user talk pages or for those who may not have read the subject's talk page. Each edit summary has a character limit of 200. Logged-in editors should mark a dummy edit as minor using the appropriate checkbox. Examples of dummy edits include altering the number of newlines in the wikitext. For instance, changing the number of newlines from 0 to 1 or from 2 to 3 does not affect the rendered page. However, changing from 1 to 2 newlines can create a visible difference, which may disqualify it as a dummy edit. Adding newlines to the end of an article does not qualify as a dummy edit either. Another example is modifying the number of spaces in the text. Changing one space to two or more spaces, or vice versa, does not alter the rendered page because multiple spaces are always displayed as a single space unless the line begins with a leading space. A null edit, on the other hand, occurs when a page is saved without any actual changes to the wikitext. This type of edit is useful for refreshing the page's cache. Unlike a dummy edit, a null edit does not create a record in the page's edit history, does not appear in Recent Changes, and does not retain an edit summary. Examples of null edits include opening the edit window and saving the page without making any changes. Saving a section edit can also result in a null edit, although it may sometimes be recorded as a dummy edit. Additionally, adding newlines only to the end of an article and saving it qualifies as a null edit.
